title: Prome Kingdom
capsule: The Prome Kingdom (Pyay, Burmese: ပြည်နယ်) arose in 1482 when Yamankan, a prince of the Hanthawaddy Pegu kingdom, established an independent power base at Prome on the Irrawaddy in central Burma following the collapse of Pegu's authority. The kingdom occupied a strategic position on the river trade route between Ava in the north and the Mon delta ports in the south, and it alternated between vassalage and conflict with the resurgent Toungoo dynasty. King Tabinshwehti of Toungoo conquered Prome around 1542, incorporating it into the first Toungoo Empire and ending its independent existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Prome Kingdom's core territory around the Irrawaddy bend is established from Burmese chronicles (Hmannan Yazawin); the kingdom's peripheral administrative reach is imprecisely known and scholarly estimates vary.
